root_motivation: A person with a spreadsheet and a Claude Pro subscription wants Claude to answer questions over their own rows, and today must either paste the CSV into every conversation or stand up Airtable/Notion plus its own MCP server (Problem statement). mcphost's own state tables (SQL-backed-in-spirit but filter-grammar-only, host.state.*, src/state.rs / src/tenant_state.rs, quotas in src/plans.rs) already exist and go unused by anyone but synthetic tenants. This PRD ships one llms.txt recipe (table_create, batched insert, publish a python query tool, connect Claude Desktop), a proof script with a 1,000-row fixture, and a synthorg task -- zero mcphost code changes: the recipe composes host.state.*/host.tool_publish exactly as they already exist.
user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) the owner's agent creates `expenses`, inserts 1,000 rows in batches, publishes `query`, and answers a question from Claude Desktop; (2) the owner adds a row from Claude and the next query sees it (host.state.insert's per-primary-key upsert already gives this for free, no extra code); (3) Joe's synthetic panel runs the recipe and sees p50 time to first answered question.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given llms.txt, When the section is read, Then it shows table_create, batched insert, the query publish, and the Desktop connection line, under 70 lines.
Given the 1,000-row fixture and a fresh tenant, When proof.sh runs, Then all rows are present (host.state.query count = 1000).
Given the published query tool, When asked the equality, range, and count questions, Then each answer matches the fixture's known value.
Given a where with op = LIKE or a raw SQL string, When query is called, Then it returns a validation error and no rows.
Given the proof completed, When signup_events is read, Then source=recipe:database-in-a-minute.
Given the proof runs against https://mcphost.dev/mcp, When it finishes, Then import is under 30 s and all assertions pass. (Live)
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: proving it needs a real run against production https://mcphost.dev/mcp, unreachable from this worktree's own gate. Embodied (gated on MCPHOST_LIVE=1, exercises the same examples/database-in-a-minute/proof.sh) by tests/mcphost_database_in_a_minute_ac08_live_test_skipped_without_env.rs's live_proof_against_real_mcphost_when_enabled, same convention as PRD-mcphost-share-a-tool-not-a-key's and PRD-mcphost-team-memory's own AC6/AC8.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the synthorg task, When run 5 times, Then 5 exact-answer completions are recorded.
Given MCPHOST_LIVE unset, When the suite runs, Then the Live test is skipped.
Given csv_import, When given the fixture text, Then the table holds 1,000 rows without the caller batching.

scope: www/llms.txt: new '## Give Claude a database in one minute' section (46 lines), placed after '## Limits and pricing' and before '## Billing (tool calls, no dashboard)' (NOT between '## Give your agents one memory' and '## Limits and pricing' -- that span is team-memory's own AC1 test's heading-to-heading window, and a section landing inside it gets silently absorbed into that test's line-count/tool-count assertions, breaking it; caught and fixed in this PRD's own history, see ambiguities_resolved). host.state.table_create(expenses, {id,category,amount,day}), a batched host.state.insert call (batch size 200 = state_ops_per_call_max, stated explicitly), host.tool_publish(query, kind=python, source omitted for space) with query's accepted-args/rejected-ops sentence, a host.tool_call example, and a Claude Desktop claude_desktop_config.json mcpServers connection block (no pre-existing Desktop-connection doc exists anywhere in this repo to link instead, unlike the PRD's technical considerations assumed -- written out in full since there was nothing shorter to point at).

examples/database-in-a-minute/proof.sh (new): one fresh tenant tagged x-mcphost-synthetic: recipe:database-in-a-minute (requirement 4); host.state.table_create; five host.state.insert batches of 200 rows read from fixture.csv; a raw host.state.query confirming 1000 rows (AC2); publishes query; asks the equality (id=777 -> amount 317.46), range (amount>300 -> 476 rows), and count (category=produce -> 200 rows) questions against fixture.csv's own deterministic generation formula; two guardrail calls (op=LIKE, a raw SQL where string) confirming both are refused. Mirrors examples/team-memory/proof.sh's helper shape (mcp_call/structured_of/json_str/has_error/mcp_call_ready).

examples/database-in-a-minute/fixture.csv (new): 1,000 deterministic rows (id 1..1000, category cycling 5 values evenly so each is exactly 200 rows, amount = round(9.99 + (id % 500) * 1.11, 2), day = ((id-1) % 28) + 1) -- generated once by a throwaway script (not committed) so the three known-answer questions in proof.sh/AC3/AC7 have exact, hand-verifiable values.

examples/database-in-a-minute/tools/query.py (new): the P0 recipe's only published tool. Validates `where` is a list of {col, op, value} objects with op in the six-symbol set (rejects a raw string outright, and rejects any other op including LIKE -- both paths raise ValueError, surfacing as tool_exception, AC4); builds the mcphost.state.query filter-grammar string (host.state.query's own `where` argument is already a small string DSL supporting exactly = != < > <= >=, src/tenant_state.rs's parse_filter -- so query.py's validation and the host's own grammar agree by construction, not by convention); queries with no host-side limit so `count` reflects every matching row before this tool's own limit (default/cap 500) truncates the returned `rows` list.

examples/database-in-a-minute/tools/csv_import.py (new, P2 requirement 8 / AC9 only -- not part of the P0 recipe in llms.txt or proof.sh): takes the whole CSV text in one call, parses it with the stdlib csv module, and loops mcphost.state.insert itself in batches of 200 (state_ops_per_call_max) so the caller never batches.

examples/database-in-a-minute/synthorg-task.yaml (new): one task, segment spreadsheet_owner, gold.tool_name=query / gold.kind=python / gold.call_check="result.count == 200" -- proposed addition for RedBaron's corpus (not merged into it, same cross-repo-scope note as share-a-tool's/team-memory's own synthorg-task.yaml).

Every python-kind test skips cleanly (sandbox::require_user_namespaces_or_ci_skip) where unprivileged user namespaces aren't available.

non_goals: Uploads larger than the free row quota (10k rows); the section states the limit rather than enforcing a new one.
Joins across tables, or aggregation beyond count/sum/avg on one column (query.py returns rows + a match count; sum/avg are not implemented in this slice).

Any change to state or python-kind code (Engineering target: zero mcphost code changes -- every file this PRD touches is under www/, examples/, tests/, agent/, scripts/gen-test-suites.sh, Cargo.toml, or CHANGELOG.md).

additional.zero_mcphost_code_changes: Engineering target states this explicitly: no src/**/*.rs edit is part of this PRD's scope. Every requirement is met by composing host.state.*/host.tool_publish exactly as they exist today, from python tool source and shell/docs/tests.
additional.state_not_table: The PRD's requirement 1 names host.state.table_create/host.state.insert (the KV/filter-grammar store, src/tenant_state.rs), not host.table.* (the real-SQL store team-memory/share-a-tool use, src/tables.rs) -- deliberate: host.state.query's own `where` argument is already a small, non-SQL filter-grammar string supporting exactly the six ops requirement 3 allows, so 'no raw SQL from the caller' (AC4) is enforced by construction on the host side too, not just by query.py's own validation.
additional.host_usage_does_not_expose_plan_quota_ma: Technical considerations says 'the proof reads rows_per_table_max/state_bytes_max from host.usage rather than hardcoding', but host.usage (src/control.rs's usage()) and billing.plans()/billing.status() (src/billing.rs) only ever report CURRENT usage against a quota, never the quota's own max value, for host.state.*'s state_rows_max/state_bytes_max/state_ops_per_call_max specifically (confirmed by reading both functions in full) -- and zero_mcphost_code_changes above forbids adding a new field to expose them. The llms.txt section states the free-plan numbers as prose (1,000 of the 10,000-row quota, batch size 200) instead; no AC asserts a runtime read of the quota maximum, only AC2's real row count and AC3's real answers, both of which are exercised against the live host, not hardcoded.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does 'I have a CSV, ask Claude about it' stay a manual, copy-paste-into-every-conversation job today?
five_whys_trace.a: The alternative is standing up Airtable or Notion plus its own MCP server and wiring auth -- too much ceremony for a one-off spreadsheet question (Problem statement).

five_whys_trace.q: Why can't mcphost's existing state-table primitive (host.state.*, src/tenant_state.rs) already serve this without any new code?
five_whys_trace.a: It can -- table_create/insert/query already exist with exactly the columns, batching, and filter-grammar this recipe needs. The gap is entirely documentation and a worked example: nothing in www/llms.txt or examples/ shows an agent using it, so state tables 'go unused by anyone but synthetic tenants' (Problem statement).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the published `query` tool need its own validation layer if host.state.query's own filter grammar already rejects anything but the six comparison ops?
five_whys_trace.a: Because host.state.query's `where` argument is a string the tool itself must BUILD from the caller's structured {col,op,value} args (requirement 3's own shape) -- the validation has to happen in query.py before that string is assembled, both so a caller-supplied LIKE/raw-SQL-string is refused with a clear tool-level error (AC4) rather than a confusing host-side parse failure, and so `columns`/`limit` (which host.state.query doesn't know about at all) are enforced somewhere.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the equality/range/count answer set need a hand-generated, deterministic fixture instead of random data?
five_whys_trace.a: AC3 requires each answer to match a 'known value' -- only possible if the fixture's generation formula is deterministic and the three questions' expected answers were computed once and hardcoded into both proof.sh and its test, the same way every other proof.sh in this repo (team-memory's WRITER=, share-a-tool's payload.ok) asserts on a value it can actually predict.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a synthorg task belong in this PRD rather than a follow-on?
five_whys_trace.a: Goal 1 promises 'CSV in, question answered, under 60 s' and the PRD's third user story asks Joe's synthetic panel to measure p50 time to first answered question -- neither claim is real until something actually times it, the same reasoning every landed recipe in this repo (share-a-tool, team-memory) already established as convention.

ambiguities_resolved.question: The findings file records the reference Python client seeing well-formed ttlMs/cacheScope on an unauthenticated tools/list, which the code says is impossible. Which is right?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Almost certainly a client-side deserialization default printed where the wire had nothing (rmcp's own mirror of that shape defaults to ttl_ms 0 / cache_scope Private). Settled by a test rather than an argument: AC2 asserts on the serialized wire JSON, not a deserialized model.
